properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 10 at 6:48AM EDT until October 10 at 8:45AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
SMWCHS

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from South Santee River to Edisto Beach out 60 NM...

* Until 845 AM EDT.

* At 648 AM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 12 NM northeast of Y-73 Reef, moving north
at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 34 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Hector Reef and Cape Romain Reef.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 3:38AM PDT until October 12 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, including the following

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 6:36AM EDT until October 10 at 9:30AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
FFWCHS

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Charleston County in southeastern South Carolina...

* Until 930 AM EDT.

* At 636 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
North Charleston, Mount Pleasant, James Island, Johns Island, West
Ashley, Downtown Charleston, Fort Sumter, Daniel Island, Folly
Beach and Kiawah Island.

Very heavy rainfall is pushing onshore around Kiawah Island and Folly
Beach, producing hourly rainfall rates up to 2 inches per hour. With
high tide approaching, the risk for flash flooding will only increase
over the next few hours. Intense rainfall will likely make travel
hazardous due to water covering roadways across Folly Beach, James
Island, Johns Island, West Ashley, and downtown Charleston.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Report flooding directly to the Charleston National Weather Service
at 1-888-383-2024 or email your reports to nws.charlestonsc@noaa.gov.

properties.areaDesc: Bryan, GA; Chatham, GA
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 6:21AM EDT until October 10 at 9:15AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Bryan County in southeastern Georgia...
Chatham County in southeastern Georgia...

* WHEN...Until 915 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 619 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- A cluster of thunderstorms will move through Chatham County and
the Savannah metro area over the next hour. Very heavy rainfall
will occur, with hourly rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour
expected. This will likely produce at least minor flooding on
area roadways. The main area of concern includes Skidaway Island,
Wilmington Island, and Savannah.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tybee Island, Midtown Savannah, Coffee Bluff, Windsor Forest,
Hunter Army Airfield, Wilmington Island, Downtown Savannah,
Hutchinson Island, Fort Pulaski National Monument and Montgomery.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Report flooding directly to the Charleston National Weather Service
at 1-888-383-2024 or email your reports to nws.charlestonsc@noaa.gov.

properties.areaDesc: Pike
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 10 at 6:20AM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
A period of strong wind gusts is expected today as the remnants
of Hurricane Isaias move into eastern Kentucky. Southeasterly
winds of 10 to 20 mph, with gusts up to 35 mph are expected. The
strongest winds are expected during the afternoon and should
coincide with the arrival of the leading bands of rain. Once
rainfall becomes steady, many areas will see the winds lighten,
except at elevations above 1,500 feet, where the gusty winds are
expected to continue into the night. Isolated gusts over 40 mph
are possible over the highest ridge tops. The gusty winds could
blow around unsecured outdoor objects and decor.

properties.areaDesc: Southeastern Elko County; Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range; White Pine County; South Central Elko County; Northwestern Nye County; Northeastern Nye County
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 3:17AM PDT until October 12 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall and debris flows
are possible.

* WHERE...Portions of eastern, northeast, and south central Nevada,
including the following areas, in eastern Nevada, White Pine. In
northeast Nevada, the Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in
Elko, South Central Elko and Southeastern Elko. In south central
Nevada, Northeastern Nye and Northwestern Nye.

* WHEN...From this evening through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. In
addition, flash flooding is possible over recently burned areas
like the former Ward Fire, Kearny Fire, Oxley Fire, Secret Pass
Fire, Star Valley Fire, Jones Fire, and Egberts Fire. Other burn
scar locations in the watch area could also be affected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture from decaying Hurricane Rachel is expected to move
northward, crossing into portions of east-central and eastern
Nevada late tonight through roughly Monday. This significant
moisture will interact with upper level low pressure to bring
widespread showers with isolated thunderstorms to the watch area.
Moderate to locally heavy rain will cause excessive runoff and
may result in rock, mud, and debris flows in and near former fire
burned areas, steep terrain, and poorly drained urban areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 10 at 6:15AM EDT until October 11 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 35 to 50 mph
expected over higher terrain above 1,500 feet and in the valleys
immediately northwest of the Pine, Black, Cumberland, and Log
Mountains. Communities at greatest risk for the strongest wind
gusts include Cumberland, Eolia, Chenoa, Frakes, and Mayking.
Locations further removed from these taller prominent mountains
should expect southeast winds of 10 to 15 mph with occasional gusts
of 20 to 35 mph.

* WHERE...Bell, Harlan, and Letcher Counties.

* WHEN...From noon today to 5 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs and weakly rooted trees in steep terrain could be blown down
and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Communities at greatest risk for the strongest
wind gusts include Cumberland, Eolia, Chenoa, Frakes, and Mayking.
Locations further removed from these taller prominent mountains
should expect southeast winds of 10 to 15 mph with occasional gusts
of 20 to 35 mph.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 4:07AM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, San
Rafael Swell, Sanpete Valley, Sevier Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book
Cliffs, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef National Park and
Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central
Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper Sevier River Valleys, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County, Southwest Utah and Zion
National Park. This also includes recent burn scars such as
Forsyth, Cottonwood, Silver King, France Canyon, and Monroe Canyon.

* WHEN...From noon MDT today through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may
occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Anomalously high moisture is forecast to impact the region with
the arrival of the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel. While this
is expected to be a long duration rainfall event, scattered
instances of heavier rainfall rates are expected with stronger
storms yielding flash flooding concerns given saturated soils and
prior burn scars.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 4:07AM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Western
Millard and Juab Counties, Bear Lake and Bear River Valley, Cache
Valley/Utah Portion, Eastern Box Elder County, Great Salt Lake
Desert and Mountains, Northern Wasatch Front, Salt Lake Valley,
Tooele and Rush Valleys, Utah Valley, Wasatch Back, Wasatch
Mountains I-80 North, Wasatch Mountains South of I-80, Western
Uinta Basin and Western Uinta Mountains. This includes recent burn
scars such as Rocky Canyon.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and recent burn scars. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage and urban areas. Extensive street flooding and flooding of
creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel
will move into northern Utah this weekend producing a prolonged
rainfall event. In particular, moisture interacting with a
frontal boundary across far northern Utah may yield locally
heavier rainfall totals compared to other locations. As a result,
areal flooding is expected across northern Utah this weekend.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
